extracted.intended_audience: clergy, church-readers, and the polite literate public (coffee-house patrons and genteel society)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance on the proper reading of the Book of Common Prayer and on public behaviour, dress, and conversation in polite society; aimed at improving elocution, deportment, and social decorum. Covers elocution techniques, posture, emphasis, anti-patterns (cant, pindarick reading), and wider rules of conduct in public places.

rubrics_metrics.name: The well Reading of the Common Prayer
rubrics_metrics.description: The well Reading of the Common Prayer is of so great Importance ... it is indeed wonderful, that the frequent Exercise of it should not make the Performers of that Duty more expert in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the liturgy as an act of worship, not a mere form; the text's excellence and affecting terms require a proper manner of delivery to have the intended influence. Examples in the text: Confession read with resigned humility; Absolution with comfortable authority; Thanksgivings with religious joy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach and attend to English reading early
rubrics_metrics.description: Reading of the English is wholly neglected... whilst Boys at School, when they are got into Latin, they are looked upon as above English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schools must instruct English reading with due observations on proper accent and manner to avoid ill habits that impede later public reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use an exemplary reader as a model
rubrics_metrics.description: The only way that I know of to remedy this, is to propose some Person of great Ability that way as a Pattern for them; Example being most effectual to convince the Learned, as well as instruct the Ignorant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a skilled reader demonstrate at public assemblies (e.g., Sion-College) so others may imitate clearness, strength, and manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read with clearness, loudness, and strength
rubrics_metrics.description: Those that are afraid of stretching their Mouths, and spoiling their soft Voice, will learn to Read with Clearness, Loudness, and Strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projected, articulate delivery so congregation/listeners can attend; combats habitual mumbling or inaudible recitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain decent behaviour and erect posture while reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Others that affect a rakish negligent Air by folding their Arms, and lolling on their Book, will be taught a decent Behaviour, and comely Erection of Body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posture affects perceived reverence and clarity; avoid slouching, folded arms, or lounging when performing public reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a deliberate pace; avoid reading too fast
rubrics_metrics.description: Those that Read so fast as if impatient of their Work, may learn to speak deliberately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberateness invites attention and reflection; rushing makes the service seem perfunctory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'Pindarick' (uneven, capricious) reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Pindarick Readers ... pronounce five or six Words with great Deliberation, and the five or six subsequent ones with as great Celerity: The first part of a Sentence with a very exalted Voice, and the latter part with a submissive one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek evenness of voice and delivery; avoid erratic alternations of tempo, volume, and tone that distract and confuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place emphasis and give the proper accent to each word
rubrics_metrics.description: May then be informed of the Art of Reading movingly and fervently, how to place the Emphasis, and give the proper Accent to each Word, and how to vary the Voice according to the Nature of the Sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize semantic weight (important words/phrases), vary tone to match sentence type (petition, thanksgiving, confession), and conclude sentences with a gentle cadence appropriate to prayer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vary voice according to the nature of the sentence; conclude with suitable cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sentence concluded with a gentle Cadence, and, in a word, with such an Accent and Turn of Speech as is peculiar to Prayer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match melodic contour and cadence to the rhetorical role of the sentence—humble, grateful, petitionary; avoid monotone or inappropriate musicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not read prayers like a Gazette or in a familiar colloquial tone
rubrics_metrics.description: There is certainly a very great Difference between the Reading a Prayer and a Gazette, ... who affect, forsooth, a certain Gentleman-like Familiarity of Tone, and mend the Language as they go on, crying instead of Pardoneth and Absolveth, Pardons and Absolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain reverence and the traditional liturgical diction; do not modernize or trivialize archaic forms out of misplaced familiarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'cant'—bawling, muttering, and whining exclamations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cant ... signifies all sudden Exclamations, Whinings, unusual Tones, and in fine all Praying and Preaching, like the unlearned of the Presbyterians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use sudden jumps, bawling, muttering, or whining tones; but note that proper elevation, emphasis, and accent are not to be considered cant when done with skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place emphasis on significant words, not on insignificant particles
rubrics_metrics.description: They make use of an Emphasis, but so improperly, that it is often placed on some very insignificant Particle, as upon if, or and.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid stressing conjunctions or particles; accent meaning-bearing words to convey sense and move the congregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public decorum: avoid making private musical performances in public places
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gentleman who constantly sings a Voluntary in spite of the whole Company ... has not been contented with that, but has danced up to the Glass in the Middle of the Room, and practised Minuet-steps to his own Humming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not impose personal amusements (singing, dancing) on mixed public assemblies such as coffee-houses; preserve public convenience and decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid loud speaking and vainglorious ostentation in mixed company
rubrics_metrics.description: Your loud Speakers: These treat Mankind as if we were all deaf; they do not express but declare themselves ... Many of these are guilty ... out of Vanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modulate volume to the room and audience; avoid assuming your words are of universal interest or forcing attention by volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not affect whispering to create false importance or spread half-accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Your Whisperer ... gets by me, and with a Whisper tells me things which all the Town knows ... Whisperers deal only in half Accounts of what they entertain you with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the affectation of secrecy as a means of seeming privy to important information; provide full accounts if you claim knowledge or else remain candidly ignorant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume silent gravity will make you seem wiser
rubrics_metrics.description: A certain Set of Ladies complain they are frequently perplexed with a Visitant who affects to be wiser than they are; which Character he hopes to preserve by an obstinate Gravity, and great Guard against discovering his Opinion upon any Occasion whatsoever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artificial silence and feigned gravity often irritate rather than impress; participate honestly in conversation rather than using taciturnity as a pose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dress appropriately; avoid pitiful or awkward attire if you seek respect
rubrics_metrics.description: Few things make a Man appear more despicable ... than an awkward or pitiful Dress; ... an awkward or pitiful Dress prejudices hearers against what he is going to offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present yourself with clean, suitable, and fitting clothing; poor dress can undermine credibility regardless of eloquence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain the medium between fop and sloven; appear rather above than below your fortune
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medium between a Fop and a Sloven is what a Man of Sense would endeavour to keep; ... Mr. Osbourn advises his Son to appear in his Habit rather above than below his Fortune.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extreme affectations (foppishness) and extreme neglect (slovenliness); modest elevation of dress procures respect and suits genteel society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid masquerading beneath your quality by under-dressing
rubrics_metrics.description: I cannot but think the old Gentleman was in some measure justly served for walking in Masquerade, I mean appearing in a Dress so much beneath his Quality and Estate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align appearance with social station; under-dressing that contradicts true status invites insult or misunderstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make pleasure the chief purpose of life
rubrics_metrics.description: When Pleasure is made the chief Pursuit of Life, it will necessarily follow that such Monsters as these will arise ... Pleasure, when it is a Man's chief Purpose, disappoints it self; and the constant Application to it palls the Faculty of enjoying it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek moderation and duties beyond immediate gratification; excess in pleasure invites moral and social ruin, irresolution, and loss of reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid extravagance, intemperance, and procrastination
rubrics_metrics.description: All the poor Rogues that make such lamentable Speeches after every Sessions at Tyburn, were, in their Way, Men of Wit and Pleasure ... Irresolution and Procrastination in all a Man's Affairs, are the natural Effects of being addicted to Pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extravagance leads to poverty and familial hardship; cultivate industry, temperance, and decisiveness to preserve honour and estate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a marriage partner for intrinsic qualities, not for fortune
rubrics_metrics.description: If you take him for his personal Perfections will sooner arrive at the Gifts of Fortune, than he whom you take for the sake of his Fortune attain to Personal Perfections. ... employ Fortune upon Certainties, but do not sacrifice Certainties to Fortune.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract suitors from their present circumstances to judge intrinsic character; prefer the man who loves you for yourself and will comfort you 'undressed' rather than one chosen principally for wealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: When men are equal, riches may be a reason for preference (practical caveat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Men are equal, there is no doubt Riches ought to be a Reason for Preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a practical tiebreaker, financial considerations are defensible when other qualities are comparable; still beware motives tied solely to fortune.
